intro: Today's digest highlights significant advancements in AI-driven hardware design, critical security patches for OpenSSL, and new language features in C# and PostgreSQL. We also explore the evolving landscape of agentic engineering and the challenges of privacy in an AI-integrated mobile ecosystem.

items.summary: OpenSSL addresses a buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() by returning -1 for invalid inputs, fixing CVE-2026-121481. Developers should update to prevent potential exploitation via large inputs.
items.why: Critical buffer overflow in OpenSSL requires immediate updates to prevent high-severity security exploits.

article.title: OpenSSL: Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8)

items.summary: Frostbite is a new CPU architecture designed and verified by AI, achieving 4.59x performance-per-watt improvement over a modern CPU core. Developers may care as it demonstrates AI's potential to co-design hardware and software, leading to significant performance gains and new architectural possibilities.
items.why: Demonstrates AI's ability to design and verify CPU architectures with massive performance-per-watt gains.

article.title: Frostbite: A new CPU architecture discovered, designed and verified by AI

items.summary: An error's code may not persist in traces despite being present in the application, affecting diagnostic accuracy. Developers should verify which error fields survive serialization to ensure reliable debugging and policy enforcement.
items.why: Crucial for debugging; developers must ensure error metadata survives serialization for reliable production tracing.

article.title: Your Error Survived the Wrapper. Did Its Code Survive the Trace?

items.summary: The article argues that reliable agentic engineering requires a factory system that verifies changes through evidence, not blind trust in agents. Developers should care because it highlights how to build systems that catch mistakes, limit their impact, and improve over time.
items.why: Provides a framework for building reliable agentic systems by prioritizing verification over blind trust.

article.title: Don't Trust the Agent. Trust the Factory.

items.summary: A language model can rewrite its own weights through self-reasoning without training or gradients, improving accuracy on unseen tasks. Developers may care as this could lead to more efficient, self-improving models that don't require retraining or external prompts.
items.why: Explores models that can autonomously modify their own weights, potentially revolutionizing self-improving software.

article.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights

items.summary: C# 15 introduces union types, offering a new way to model data with compiler-checked exhaustive matching. Developers can experiment with these features using a .NET 11 playground repository on GitHub.
items.why: C# 15 union types offer a safer, compiler-checked way to model complex data structures.

article.title: C# 15 Unpacked: Unions Have Arrived. Here's Why They Matter

items.summary: PostgreSQL 19 introduces new SQL features like IGNORE NULLS and JSONPath transformations, along with improved replication and maintenance tools. Developers can test these features in a live sandbox environment with real PostgreSQL 19 servers.
items.why: PostgreSQL 19 introduces significant SQL improvements and JSONPath transformations for better data handling.

article.title: PostgreSQL 19: A hands-on tour with runnable browser examples

items.summary: Signal is blocking AI agents on iOS 27 and Android from accessing its app data to protect user privacy. Developers care because these OS-level AI integrations threaten app-level privacy and require new tools to prevent data exposure.
items.why: Highlights the growing conflict between OS-level AI integrations and application-level data privacy.

article.title: Signal Is Serious About Protecting Your Privacy

items.summary: A Docker container marked unhealthy continued serving traffic because health checks don't affect traffic routing or restart policies. Developers should understand that health checks only report status, not enforce behavior, requiring additional orchestration for failover.
items.why: Clarifies a common misconception: Docker health checks do not automatically stop traffic routing.

article.title: Marking a container unhealthy didn't stop it from taking traffic
article.summary: I broke a container on purpose and watched Docker mark it unhealthy for 35 seconds while nginx kept sending it a third of all traffic. The actual cause: a missing http_500 in proxy_next_upstream.

items.summary: An unofficial ggml backend, ggml-tpu, allows running llama.cpp on Google Cloud TPU by compiling its graph into XLA programs. Developers can leverage TPUs for faster inference with minimal changes to their llama.cpp setup.
items.why: Enables running llama.cpp on Cloud TPUs via XLA for high-performance inference scaling.

article.title: llama.cpp on a Cloud TPU: An Unofficial ggml Backend Through XLA
article.summary: ggml-tpu lowers each llama.cpp graph to one StableHLO program, compiles it with XLA and runs it on a TPU through libtpu. Gemma 4 E2B on one TPU v5e chip: build, test every operation, serve, chat, speculative decoding, and a three-cell Colab notebook.
